newsitem.title: USA: Rochester G&E, Niagara Mohawk plan nuclear venture.
newsitem.headline: Rochester G&E, Niagara Mohawk plan nuclear venture.

text.p: Rochester Gas and Electric Corp said it plans to form a joint nuclear operating company with Niagara Mohawk Power Corp to support and manage the operations of RG&E's Ginna nuclear plant and Niagara Mohawk's Nine Mile Point One and Two plants.

The plan includes formation of a nuclear services company -- named New York Nuclear Operating Co -- to provide support services such as quality assessment, engineering support, emergency preparedness, fuel management and others. Ultimately, the plan calls for the creation of a joint operating company to manage the three plants, Rochester said.

Long Island Lighting Co, New York State Electric and Gas Corp and Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp, co-owners of Nine Mile Two along with RG&E and Niagara Mohawk, support the joint operating venture.

Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc, owner and operator to the Indian Point Two plant, has expressed an interest in joining with the two utilities and is expected to make a decision in the near future, Rochester said.
The New York Power Authority, owner and operator of the James A. Fitzpatrick nuclear plant and the Indian Point 3 nuclear plant, has been urged to participate, Rochester said.
B. Ralph Sylvia, Niagara Mohawk's executive vice-president and chief nuclear officer, has been selected to initially head the formation of the nuclear services and operating company.

The "ultimate idea" of the joint operating structure is that the licenses for operation of the plants could be transferred to the new venture if New York regulators decide that generation should be divested from ownership of transmission facilities as part of the electric utility industry restructuring now being studied, RG&E spokesman Mike Power said.
In a joint letter to New York Power Authority Chairman Clarence Rappleyea, the chief executives of the two utilities, Roger W. Kober and William E. Davis, invited the Power Authority to participate.
They said NYPA's involvement in the formation of a statewide nuclear services and operating company would benefit New York's electricity consumers.

"The operating company provides both the focus required to be successful in the nuclear business coupled with the ability to share resources to ensure the long-term success of our nuclear facilities," Niagara Mohawk's Davis said.
"Additionally, all of the benefits will be retained by companies whose homes are in New York State."

Entergy Corp's selection to operate NYPA's nuclear plants, now being discussed by the authority, would not preclude NYPA's participation in the operating company, Power said. They could bring Entergy on board with them, he noted.

Niagara Mohawk is the owner and operator of Nine Mile Point One, a 620-megawatt plant. Nine Mile Two, a 1,180-megawatt plant operated by Niagara Mohawk, is jointly owned by Niagara Mohawk (41 percent), RG&E (14 percent), Lilco (18 percent), New York State Electric and Gas (18 percent) and Central Hudson (9 percent). Both plants are located in Scriba, N.Y.
RG&E is the owner and operator of the Ginna nuclear plant, a 470-megawatt plant located in Ontario, N.Y.
Con Edison's Indian Point 2 is a 975 megawatt plant while the New York Power Authority's Indian Point 3 has a 980 megawatt capacity and Fitzpatrick 800 megawatts.
